title: opum-sdlc: a deliberate tracker write gets its own PR, not a ride-along
summary: Candidate rule for opum-sdlc, from opum-agent, to land in the same stacked release as OMARK-25's auto-merge rule. Not to be started now. Prompted by this session's own OMARK-26 finding: `quest task complete` moves a task's record into `.quest/completed/` -- a tracked file change like any other -- but it was run directly on a bare `dev` checkout with no branch of its own, right after OMARK-26's work PR had already merged. It sat uncommitted through OMARK-27's entire branch/commit/merge cycle, invisible to origin, caught only because `git status` flagged it on the next `dev` sync. The failure mode is severe precisely because the work itself was correct: only the EVIDENCE of completion was lost. An auditor sees a merged PR and a task still marked open and cannot tell whether the work was done, abandoned, or half-finished -- this repo's own estate would have reported OMARK-26 as open. THE INTERACTION opum-agent flagged, which is why this is a rule and not just a habit fix: the OMARK-23 interim mitigation opum-agent gave the whole fleet this morning -- 'nobody opens a PR whose entire content is a hook-written note; let it ride along with the next substantive commit' -- trains exactly the habit that lost this completion. It teaches sessions that an uncommitted tracker change sitting in the working tree is a normal, expected state to be picked up later, and a `quest task complete` sitting uncommitted looks identical to a hook note sitting uncommitted. One is designed to ride; the other is a record of work that will silently not exist if it is never committed. THE RULE, with both halves: hook-written boilerplate (SessionEnd/PreCompact's automatic note) may ride along with the next substantive commit; a deliberate tracker write -- a completion, a status change, a note a session itself authored -- gets its own branch and PR like any other change. The distinguishing test is WHO WROTE IT, not what file it touches.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Add the two-part rule to opum-sdlc as prose placed near wherever tracker chores and the branch-and-PR path are already described -- the existing 'Tracker-only and docs-only chores take this same path' text in Deliver is the natural anchor, since this rule is a clarification of exactly that path rather than a new mechanism. Final placement is this task's call to make with the SKILL.md text in front of them, not settled here.

State the failure mode plainly alongside the rule, not just the prohibition: a deliberate tracker write left uncommitted is indistinguishable, to a later git status or an estate audit, from work that was never done -- the OMARK-26 incident is the concrete case to cite.

Name the distinguishing test explicitly in the rule text: WHO wrote the change (the hook, automatically, vs. a session, deliberately), not WHAT file it touches -- both can touch the same .quest/tasks/*.json file, which is why 'which file' is not a usable test.

Land in the same release that carries OMARK-23's fix and OMARK-25's auto-merge rule (all three ride opum-workflow's CHANGELOG Unreleased section per the current release hold, dated to close 2026-09-15) rather than as a separate standalone version bump.

implementationNotes: Filed at opum-agent's (orchestrator) request, 2026-09-09. Not to be started now -- explicitly captured for the record so it survives to the next deliberate opum-workflow release, same as OMARK-25.

Cross-reference: a line was added to OMARK-23's own notes recording this interaction, since OMARK-23's interim mitigation is what created the ambiguity this task documents, and OMARK-23's actual shipped fix (skip the hook note when nothing changed) partly retires the ambiguity at the source rather than by documentation -- the two tasks address the same root cause from different angles (mechanism vs. habit) and neither makes the other unnecessary.

This is a skills/ change once implemented, so it will trip check . manifests' content-changed guard the same way OMARK-23, OMARK-25, and OMARK-26 (the CLAUDE.md edit) did or would have -- another Unreleased CHANGELOG entry, not a version bump, for the same release-hold reason.
